arguments.name: Participant-specific defeat and the justice objection
arguments.position: Developed Adams internal-coherence defense; serious direct Sutherland criticism and limited revised-response dossier
premises: Horror prima facie threatens a participant’s life as a good to that participant.
Divine goodness includes goodness to each person, not only a global total.
On the selected Christian scheme, divine intimacy and integration could defeat that threat.
bridge_principles: Meaningful integration and sufficient goodness to each participant could establish compossibility even without access to divine permission reasons.
Continued same-person life, adequate goods and coherent intimacy remain required.
arguments.conclusion: Adams argues for conditional internal compatibility; actual restoration and adequate original permission are not established here.
arguments.strongest_objection: Sutherland pp318–323: eventual reassurance does not decide justice of the original treatment or settle other victims’ claims; moral perception may be distorted.
arguments.strongest_reply: Revised Adams reproduction PDF2,5–6 explicitly affirms objective scope, gives a reason for whole-life value, and denies that defeat erases injustice or undermines moral judgment. This answers a claimed entailment, not every permission burden.
arguments.reply_chronology: 1989 symposium original and direct challenge; added responses explicitly named in deficient-provenance reproduction. Exact1990print unavailable; no separately dated1989rebuttal fabricated.
unresolved_issues: Adequate antecedent permission and each victim’s genuine restoration
Conceptual Christology/shared pain and personal continuity
Uninspected later monograph and complete alternative-theodicy chains

arguments.name: Temporary nonbelief for ownership and fittingness of love
arguments.position: Howard-Snyder defense tested by Schellenberg’s actual1996 response
premises: Reasonable belief makes the specified explicit relationship possible but does not equal love.
Freely owning and improving love may be goods.
For selected dispositions, withholding belief may be no worse a means than available alternatives.
bridge_principles: Stipulated prima facie permission criterion; must distinguish actual all-things-considered permission.
Epistemic restraint about unknown reasons differs from proof of a sufficient actual reason.
arguments.conclusion: A qualified challenge to confidence that no reason for temporary nonbelief exists; not an explanation of every actual nonbeliever or cultural distribution.
arguments.strongest_objection: Schellenberg pp460–462: development, confirmation and choosing continuation may occur after belief with additional benefits; no-worse comparative premise and human-lover analogy are challenged.
arguments.strongest_reply: Howard-Snyder’s earlier internal replies pp448–451 distinguish ownership from fittingness, improvement from perfection and prima facie from conclusive reasons; p453 offers an epistemic fallback. These are available defenses already in the1996article, NOT a later reply to Schellenberg1996. No such later rebuttal inspected.
arguments.reply_chronology: Howard-Snyder1996 follows his earlier critique of Schellenberg1993; Schellenberg1996 is the actual directly inspected response. Neither replies to2025.
unresolved_issues: No later H-S reply to this actual response inspected
Note18 and sufficiently fitting seeker concessions
No population psychology or actual divine reasons

arguments.name: Positive support for divine intention versus an independent no-reason premise
arguments.position: Schellenberg’s structural reply and the surviving epistemic dispute
premises: There may be positive defeasible support that a perfectly loving God intends the relevant access.
The absence of a defeating counterconsideration need not be used as an independent inductive proof that no reason exists.
Actual overriding reasons would defeat the positive claim; the negative existential is nevertheless entailed if that claim is true.
bridge_principles: Positive support must be adequate and not beg the disputed divine-intention premise.
Accepting an entailed proposition differs from independently establishing it through absence of known alternatives.
arguments.conclusion: The target of Howard-Snyder’s fallback depends on which argument is defended; no full positive case or metaphysical conclusion is established by this distinction alone.
arguments.strongest_objection: Howard-Snyder pp433–439,453: desire for access does not by itself show an all-things-considered intention; inaccessible reasons may remain.
arguments.strongest_reply: Schellenberg pp457–459 appeals to positive support, accepts defeaters and the negative existential commitment, but rejects requiring an independent Rowe-style inference.
arguments.reply_chronology: Actual1996response directly addresses the1996reconstruction; earlier1993positive argument remains a cited uninspected dependency.
unresolved_issues: Adequacy of divine-intention and human-analogy premises
Scope cost for positive goodness recognition
No complete hiddenness exchange or family verdict
